45.description: Saskatoon City Council recognized Marvin Dutton for over 20 years of volunteer service on the Board of Revision, acknowledging his lasting impact on the committee and residents.

42.description: Council approved changes to the bylaw that governs private sewer and water service connections in Saskatoon.

chips.text: City Solicitor requested to prepare the specific bylaw amendments.

43.description: Saskatoon will apply for federal funding to support urban forestry plans and studies. If successful, $100,000 will be added to the Tree Replacement and Urban Forest Enhancement project.

chips.text: City will apply to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities Green Municipal Fund.

41.description: Saskatoon's Environmental Advisory Committee provided its 2025 annual report on local environmental matters to City Council.

51.description: Saskatoon will amend Council Policy C07-025 to update loading zone regulations, incorporating findings from the Accessible Loading Zone Pilot.

chips.text: Enhances accessibility for residents needing loading zones.

49.description: Saskatoon City Council approved capital project funding for cultural projects recommended by the Cultural Grant Capital Reserve Assessment Committee for 2026.

chips.text: Cultural organizations will receive capital project funding for 2026.

50.description: City Council acknowledged the 2025 annual report for the Marr Residence, a local historic site.

46.description: Council approved borrowing up to $124,845,000 for 2026 capital projects, including water treatment, transit, new water mains, and indoor recreation facilities.

chips.text: $7.8M for the Indoor Recreation Facilities Project
Taxpayers will fund up to $124,845,000 in capital projects through borrowing.

47.description: Saskatoon will provide funding to the Saskatoon Regional Economic Development Authority (SREDA) for services from 2026 to 2029.

48.description: Saskatoon will withdraw $195,933.86 from the Property Realized Reserve to cover land development and sales costs from December 2024 to November 2025.

56.description: Council approved electrical rate increases for Saskatoon Light & Power, effective February 1, 2026, and February 1, 2027.

chips.text: Saskatoon Light & Power customers will be affected by the rate increases.

57.description: Doug Daniels was appointed to the Development Appeals Board, with his term extending until the end of 2027.

58.description: Council appointed Councillors Dubois, Timon, Donauer, and Jeffries to P4G planning and oversight committees for 2026, and Harrison Oboghor for a three-year term.

59.description: Walker Paterson was appointed to the Saskatoon Public Library Board of Directors, serving as a citizen representative until the end of 2027.

60.description: Saskatoon City Council appointed Cheryl Ermine, representing Saskatoon Public Schools, to the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Advisory Committee until the end of 2026.

chips.text: The appointment supports the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Advisory Committee's work.

61.description: Karthik Babu Menon is reappointed to the Saskatoon Accessibility Advisory Committee, representing Spinal Cord Injury Saskatchewan Inc., until the end of 2027.

chips.text: Ensures continued representation for people with accessibility needs.

62.description: Gary Beaudin will continue representing the United Way on the Social Services Subcommittee until the end of 2026.

63.description: Michael Lewis was appointed to the Municipal Heritage Advisory Committee as the Saskatoon Archaeology Society representative until the end of 2027.

55.description: Saskatoon will fund Discover Saskatoon from 2026-2029 with annual inflationary increases, a $100,000 performance bonus, and $50,000 for major events, while exploring tourism governance reforms.

chips.text: City Manager stressed hotels must remain primary decision-makers for Discover Saskatoon funding.
Saskatoon taxpayers and 13,000 tourism jobs are impacted by this funding.
Discover Saskatoon CEO warned the motion might constrain the system that generates demand.
Administration committed to considering the Ottawa model for future tourism funding governance.

53.description: Saskatoon reallocated $21.6 million to upsize water and wastewater infrastructure for regional growth, with costs recovered from future development.

chips.text: The project supports regional growth for 80,000 people or heavy industrial users in the P4G area.
Staff could not identify the specific cause of current increased sewer odors in the north end.
New pipeline design includes aeration to reduce hydrogen sulfide, a repugnant smell from wastewater.
The city promises to fully recover the investment through development levies from future growth.

44.description: City Council is considering a bylaw to provide a tax exemption for the Saskatchewan Housing Corporation, allowing for a public hearing on the matter.

chips.text: Councillor Dunner asked if a motion to direct work aligned with prior staff commitments.

54.description: Council initiated the process to amend the Electric Light and Power Bylaw, allowing for a public hearing on the proposed changes.

40.description: Council directed administration to explore options for monitoring winter road maintenance contractors, assessing their performance, and using past performance in future contract awards to ensure consistent service city-wide.

chips.text: Bus riders and pedestrians are affected by uncleared bus stops and sidewalks.
Speaker questioned if 'winter road' definition includes bus stops and pedestrian areas.
Bus Riders of Saskatoon reported over 50,000 views on snow clearing posts
Uncleared bus stops and high snow windrows impact people with mobility issues.

52.description: The motion asks administration to study and report on key planning aspects for the Downtown Event and Entertainment District (DEED), including a district energy system, residential units, and partnerships with Indigenous nations.

chips.text: District energy system could serve new DEED facilities and other downtown buildings.
